page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.16xlarge is a high-clock-speed compute instance designed for computational tasks requiring elevated single-thread and parallel performance. Built on the KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6462C processors clocked at 3.3 GHz. Across its 64 dedicated vCPUs, it pairs 256 GB of system RAM, yielding an exact ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration avoids the memory constraints typical of hyper-dense compute profiles while preserving sustained processor throughput.

The instance provides a high-speed networking interface delivering up to 64 Gbps of baseline bandwidth, ensuring rapid network data transfers in distributed cluster environments. However, the hardware specification includes no bundled local disk storage and zero integrated GPU accelerators. Consequently, all persistent storage operations depend entirely on remote cloud-attached block volumes. Deployments must account for network storage latency, as all disk input and output will traverse the storage fabric rather than direct-attached solid-state media. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Qualitatively, the ecs.hfg8i.16xlarge provides strong resource efficiency for infrastructure designs needing predictable compute frequency across high core counts without the overhead of massive, unused memory tiers. Its balance of 64 dedicated cores and 64 Gbps network throughput makes it optimal for distributed analytics engines, high-concurrency enterprise web serving, compilation clusters, batch processing, and continuous integration workflows.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.16xlarge is a high-clock-speed instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Driven by Intel Xeon 6462C processors running at a 3.3 GHz base frequency, it delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance includes a robust 64 Gbps baseline network throughput to accommodate data-heavy inter-node communication. It features no local NVMe or SSD storage and lacks hardware GPU acceleration, requiring cloud-attached network block storage for persistent data management. From an architectural perspective, the provision of high sustained CPU clock speeds across a wide core count offers strong compute efficiency for workloads that require heavy thread processing without overcommitting RAM. The ecs.hfg8i.16xlarge is positioned for compute-intensive enterprise operations, including batch processing, distributed data processing, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
